core.title: Cultivar: A Contrastive and Locale-Oriented Translation Benchmark for Investigating Contamination and Localisation Robustness
affiliations: Spoken Language Systems (LSV) group, Saarland University
core.summary: This work advocates for source-contrastive evaluation and instantiates Cultivar, a localised subset of FLORES, which enables locale-specific translation evaluation and finds that MT-specialised models are less robust, a few models potentially overfit FLORES, and models tend to translate US content better than that of other locales, regardless of language.

core.title: Omnilingual MT: Machine Translation for 1,600 Languages
core.venue: arXiv.org
core.summary: This work presents Omnilingual Machine Translation (OMT), the first MT system supporting more than 1,600 languages, and explores two ways of specializing a Large Language model for machine translation: as a decoder-only model (OMT-LLaMA) or as a module in an encoder-decoder architecture (OMT-NLLB).

core.title: Multilingual Reasoning Cascades Need More Context
core.venue: arXiv.org
core.summary: The need to better design information flow in machine translation cascades for mitigating error propagation is emphasized, and a simple and actionable default strategy is provided: preserve the original user question until the end of the pipeline.

core.title: There is No Theoretical Curse of Multilinguality For Embedding Space Structure
core.summary: It is shown that the minimum dimensionality required for perfect multilinguality grows only logarithmically in the number of languages, which suggests that the empirical curse of multilinguality is a result of real world data and training conditions.

core.title: Rashid: A Cipher-Based Framework for Exploring In-Context Language Learning
core.venue: arXiv.org
core.summary: A framework for studying ICLL is introduced wherein it reversibly cipher high-resource languages (HRLs) to construct truly unseen languages with access to a wide range of resources available for HRLs, unlocking previously impossible exploration of ICLL phenomena.

core.title: The Translation Barrier Hypothesis: Multilingual Generation with Large Language Models Suffers from Implicit Translation Failure
core.venue: IJCNLP-AACL
core.summary: The extent to which either stage in the pipeline is responsible for final failure for a word translation task across 108 language pairs is quantified, and the translation barrier explains a dominant portion of error for a majority of language pairs, and is especially severe for low-resource target languages.

core.title: DialUp! Modeling the Language Continuum by Adapting Models to Dialects and Dialects to Models
core.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
core.summary: DialUp is presented, consisting of a training-time technique for adapting a pretrained model to dialectal data (M->D), and an inference-time intervention adapting dialectal data to the model expertise (D->M), which shows considerable performance gains for several dialects from four language families, and modest gains for two other language families.

core.title: ChiKhaPo: A Large-Scale Multilingual Benchmark for Evaluating Lexical Comprehension and Generation in Large Language Models
core.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
core.summary: ChiKhaPo is introduced, consisting of 8 subtasks of varying difficulty designed to evaluate the lexical comprehension and generation abilities of generative models, and provides coverage for 2700+ languages for 2 subtasks, surpassing any existing benchmark in terms of language coverage.

core.title: JHU IWSLT 2025 Low-resource System Description
core.venue: International Workshop on Spoken Language Translation

core.title: How Important is 'Perfect' English for Machine Translation Prompts?
core.venue: Conference of the European Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics
core.summary: Qualitative analysis reveals that lower prompt quality largely leads to poorer instruction following, rather than directly affecting translation quality itself, and large language models can still translate in scenarios with overwhelming random noise that would make the prompt illegible to humans.

core.title: LID Models are Actually Accent Classifiers: Implications and Solutions for LID on Accented Speech
core.venue: Interspeech
core.summary: A common failure mode on accented speech whereby LID systems often misclassify L2 accented speech as the speaker's native language or a related language is identified and evidence suggesting that state-of-the-art models are invariant to permutations of short spans of speech is presented.

core.title: Pointer-Generator Networks for Low-Resource Machine Translation: Don’t Copy That!
core.venue: First Workshop on Insights from Negative Results in NLP
core.summary: This work calls for better scrutiny of linguistically motivated improvements to NMT given the blackbox nature of Transformer models, as well as for a focus on the above problems in the field.

core.title: JHU IWSLT 2024 Dialectal and Low-resource System Description
core.venue: International Workshop on Spoken Language Translation
core.summary: The results show that the best-performing approach differs by language pairs, but that fine-tuned SeamlessM4T v2 tends to perform best for source languages on which it was pre-trained.

core.title: Evaluating Large Language Models along Dimensions of Language Variation: A Systematik Invesdigatiom uv Cross-lingual Generalization
core.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
core.summary: This framework offers a cheap solution for estimating task performance on an unseen CRL given HRLN performance using its posteriors, as well as for diagnosing observed PD on a CRL in terms of its linguistic distances from its HRLN, and opens doors to principled methods of mitigating performance degradation.

core.title: Cross-lingual Strategies for Low-resource Language Modeling: A Study on Five Indic Dialects
core.venue: JEPTALNRECITAL
core.summary: This study compares some canonical strategies in language modeling for low-resource scenarios, evaluating all models by their performance on a POS-tagging downstream task and finds that a model pretrained on other mid-resource Indic dialects and languages, with extended pretraining on target dialect data, consistently outperforms other models.

core.title: When Your Cousin Has the Right Connections: Unsupervised Bilingual Lexicon Induction for Related Data-Imbalanced Languages
core.venue: International Conference on Language Resources and Evaluation
core.summary: This work presents a new method for unsupervised BLI between a related LRL and HRL that only requires inference on a masked language model of the HRL, and demonstrates its effectiveness on truly low-resource languages Bhojpuri and Magahi (with <5M monolingual tokens each), against Hindi.

core.title: Subword-based Cross-lingual Transfer of Embeddings from Hindi to Marathi and Nepali
core.venue: Special Interest Group on Computational Morphology and Phonology Workshop
core.summary: This work introduces a novel technique for static subword embeddings transfer for Indic languages from a relatively higher resource language to a genealogically related low resource language.

core.title: Combining Noisy Semantic Signals with Orthographic Cues: Cognate Induction for the Indic Dialect Continuum
core.venue: Conference on Computational Natural Language Learning
core.summary: This work presents a novel method for unsupervised cognate/borrowing identification from monolingual corpora designed for low and extremely low resource scenarios, based on combining noisy semantic signals from joint bilingual spaces with orthographic cues modelling sound change, which outperforms both traditional orthography baselines as well as EM-style learnt edit distance matrices.

core.title: Towards Universal Segmentations: UniSegments 1.0
core.venue: International Conference on Language Resources and Evaluation
core.summary: This work presents a survey of 17 existing data resources relevant for segmentation in 32 languages, and analyzes diversity of how individual linguistic phenomena are captured across them.

core.title: Clause Final Verb Prediction in Hindi: Evidence for Noisy Channel Model of Communication
core.venue: Workshop on Cognitive Modeling and Computational Linguistics
core.summary: This work presents three computational models to predict clause final verbs in Hindi given its prior arguments that differ in their use of prior context during the prediction process – the context is either noisy or noise-free.

core.title: Constrained Decoding for Technical Term Retention in English-Hindi MT
core.venue: ICON
core.summary: This work presents an English-to-Hindi model that is trained to obey a “retain” signal, i.e. it can perform the required code-mixing on a list of terms, possibly unseen, provided at runtime.

core.title: Towards Handling Verb Phrase Ellipsis in English-Hindi Machine Translation
core.venue: ICON
core.summary: This is the first attempt to target ellipsis resolution in the context of improving English-Hindi machine translation, based on an understanding of the syntactical phenomenon of verb-stranding verb phraseEllipsis in Hindi (VVPE).

core.title: On the Evaluation Practices in Multilingual NLP: Can Machine Translation Offer an Alternative to Human Translations?
core.venue: arXiv.org
core.summary: An analysis of existing evaluation frameworks in multilingual NLP, discuss their limitations, and propose several directions for more robust and reliable evaluation practices is presented.
core.source: On the Evaluation Practices in Multilingual NLP: Can Machine Translation Offer an Alternative to Human Translations?

core.title: Allocating Large Vocabulary Capacity for Cross-Lingual Language Model Pre-Training
core.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
core.summary: This work proposes k-NN-based target sampling to accelerate the expensive softmax and shows that the multilingual vocabulary learned with VoCap benefits cross-lingual language model pre-training.
core.source: Allocating Large Vocabulary Capacity for Cross-Lingual Language Model Pre-Training

core.title: MANTa: Efficient Gradient-Based Tokenization for End-to-End Robust Language Modeling
core.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
core.source: MANTa: Efficient Gradient-Based Tokenization for End-to-End Robust Language Modeling

core.title: KinyaBERT: a Morphology-aware Kinyarwanda Language Model
core.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
core.summary: A simple yet effective two-tier BERT architecture that leverages a morphological analyzer and explicitly represents morphological compositionality is proposed, naming the proposed model architecture KinyaBERT.
core.source: KinyaBERT: a Morphology-aware Kinyarwanda Language Model

core.title: MAD-G: Multilingual Adapter Generation for Efficient Cross-Lingual Transfer
core.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
core.summary: MAD-G is proposed, which contextually generates language adapters from language representations based on typological features and remains competitive with more expensive methods for language-speciﬁc adapter training across the board.
core.source: MAD-G: Multilingual Adapter Generation for Efficient Cross-Lingual Transfer

core.title: Understanding Multilingualism in Mixture-of-Experts LLMs: Routing Mechanism, Expert Specialization, and Layerwise Steering
core.venue: arXiv.org
core.summary: A routing-guided steering method is proposed that adaptively guides routing behavior in middle layers toward shared experts associated with dominant languages at inference time, leading to consistent multilingual performance improvements, particularly for linguistically related language pairs.
core.source: Understanding Multilingualism in Mixture-of-Experts LLMs: Routing Mechanism, Expert Specialization, and Layerwise Steering

core.title: The Unreasonable Effectiveness of Model Merging for Cross-Lingual Transfer in LLMs
core.venue: Proceedings of the 5th Workshop on Multilingual Representation Learning (MRL 2025)
core.summary: This work investigates cross-lingual transfer to lower-resource languages where task-specific post-training data is scarce and identifies the most consistently successful modular method to be fine-tuning separate language and math experts and model merging via Layer-Swapping.
core.source: The Unreasonable Effectiveness of Model Merging for Cross-Lingual Transfer in LLMs

core.title: Enhancing Multilingual LLM Pretraining with Model-Based Data Selection
core.venue: Neural Information Processing Systems
core.summary: A model-based filtering framework for multilingual datasets that aims to identify a diverse set of structured and knowledge-rich samples that can match the baseline MMLU score with as little as 15% of the training tokens while also improving across other benchmarks and mitigating the curse of multilinguality.

core.title: LIMIT: Language Identification, Misidentification, and Translation using Hierarchical Models in 350+ Languages
core.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
core.summary: This work takes a step towards tackling the data bottleneck by compiling a corpus of over 50K parallel children's stories in 350+ languages and dialects, and the computation bottleneck by building lightweight hierarchical models for language identification.

core.title: Balancing Training for Multilingual Neural Machine Translation
core.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
core.summary: Experiments show the proposed method not only consistently outperforms heuristic baselines in terms of average performance, but also offers flexible control over the performance of which languages are optimized.

core.title: Tokenization and Representation Biases in Multilingual Models on Dialectal NLP Tasks
core.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
core.summary: This work correlates Tokenization Parity and Information Parity, as measures of representational biases in pre-trained multilingual models, with the downstream performance, and reveals that TP is a better predictor of the performance on tasks reliant on syntactic and morphological cues, while IP better predicts performance in semantic tasks.

core.title: Hyperpolyglot LLMs: Cross-Lingual Interpretability in Token Embeddings
core.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
core.summary: This research opens the door for investigations in 1) The effect of pre-training and model architectures on representations of languages and 2) The applications of cross-lingual representations embedded in language models.

core.title: Multilingual Pixel Representations for Translation and Effective Cross-lingual Transfer
core.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
core.summary: This work introduces and demonstrates how to effectively train multilingual machine translation models with pixel representations and explores various properties of pixel representations such as parameter sharing within and across scripts to better understand where they lead to positive transfer.

core.title: Enhancing Cross-Lingual Transfer through Reversible Transliteration: A Huffman-Based Approach for Low-Resource Languages
core.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
core.summary: Experimental results demonstrate that the innovatively combines character transliteration with Huffman coding to design a complete transliteration framework significantly enhances the model's capability to process low-resource languages while maintaining performance on high-resource languages.

core.title: Condensing Multilingual Knowledge with Lightweight Language-Specific Modules
core.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
core.summary: This work shows that the LMS method significantly outperforms previous LS methods and MoE methods with the same amount of extra parameters, e.g., 1.73 BLEU points over the Switch Transformer on many-to-many multilingual machine translation.

core.title: Translate-R1: Cost-Aware Translation Tool Use via Reinforcement Learning
core.venue: arXiv.org
core.summary: This work learns a single policy that decides when to translate from reward alone, developing language- and domain-adaptive introspection that invokes translation only when it cannot solve a task natively.

core.title: Tracing Multilingual Factual Knowledge Acquisition in Pretraining
affiliations: Centre for Information and Language Processing, LMU Munich
core.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
core.summary: This work traces how factual recall and crosslingual consistency evolve during pretraining, focusing on OLMo-7B as a case study and finds that both accuracy and consistency improve over time for most languages.

core.title: Probing the Emergence of Cross-lingual Alignment during LLM Training
core.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
core.summary: A high correlation between neuron overlap and downstream performance, which supports the hypothesis on the conditions leading to effective cross-lingual transfer and detects a degradation of both implicit alignment and multilingual abilities in certain phases of the pre-training process.

core.title: ATLAS: Adaptive Transfer Scaling Laws for Multilingual Pretraining, Finetuning, and Decoding the Curse of Multilinguality
core.venue: arXiv.org
core.summary: The Adaptive Transfer Scaling Law (ATLAS) is introduced for both monolingual and multilingual pretraining, which outperforms existing scaling laws' out-of-sample generalization often by more than 0.3 R^2.

core.title: Improving In-context Learning of Multilingual Generative Language Models with Cross-lingual Alignment
affiliations: the Institute of Automation Chinese Academy of Sciences
National Laboratory of Pattern Recognition, Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences
core.venue: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics
core.summary: A simple yet effective cross-lingual alignment framework exploiting pairs of translation sentences aligns the internal sentence representations across different languages via multilingual contrastive learning and aligns outputs by following cross-lingual instructions in the target language.

core.title: Gradient Vaccine: Investigating and Improving Multi-task Optimization in Massively Multilingual Models
core.venue: International Conference on Learning Representations
core.summary: This work derives a simple and scalable optimization procedure, named Gradient Vaccine, which encourages more geometrically aligned parameter updates for close tasks and reveals the importance of properly measuring and utilizing language proximity in multilingual optimization, and has broader implications for multi-task learning beyond multilingual modeling.

core.title: MT-R1-Zero: Advancing LLM-based Machine Translation via R1-Zero-like Reinforcement Learning
core.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
core.summary: This work introduces MT-R1-Zero, the first open-source adaptation of the R1-Zero RL framework for MT without supervised fine-tuning or cold-start, and proposes a rule-metric mixed reward mechanism to guide LLMs towards improved translation quality via emergent reasoning.

core.title: Multilingual Instruction Tuning With Just a Pinch of Multilinguality
core.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
core.summary: This work investigates how multilinguality during instruction tuning of a multilingual LLM affects instruction-following across languages from the pre-training corpus, and suggests that building massively multilingual instruction-tuned models can be done with only a very small set of multilingual instruction-responses.

core.title: Causes and Cures for Interference in Multilingual Translation
core.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
core.summary: This work identifies the main factors that contribute to interference in multilingual machine translation and shows that tuning the sampling temperature to control the proportion of each language pair in the data is key to balancing the amount of interference between low and high resource language pairs effectively.

core.title: The Geometry of Low-Resource Language Representations
core.summary: It is established that the representational geometry of low- and high-resource languages in LLMs is measurably distinct, and that targeted geometric intervention is a viable strategy for improving CPT for low-resource languages.

core.title: IsoVec: Controlling the Relative Isomorphism of Word Embedding Spaces
core.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
core.summary: This work addresses the root-cause of faulty cross-lingual mapping: that word embedding training resulted in the underlying spaces being non-isomorphic, and incorporates global measures of isomorphism directly into the skipgram loss function, successfully increasing the relative isomorphicism of trained word embeding spaces and improving their ability to be mapped to a shared cross-lingsual space.

core.title: Exploring Alignment in Shared Cross-lingual Spaces
core.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
core.summary: This study encompasses three multilingual models and three downstream tasks and employs clustering to uncover latent concepts within multilingual models, focusing on quantifying the alignment and overlap of these concepts across various languages within the latent space.

core.title: Shared Global and Local Geometry of Language Model Embeddings
core.venue: arXiv.org
core.summary: This work finds numerous geometric similarities across the token embeddings of large language models and introduces EMB2EMB, a simple application to linearly transform steering vectors from one language model to another, despite the two models having different dimensions.

core.title: Discovering Low-rank Subspaces for Language-agnostic Multilingual Representations
core.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
core.summary: A novel view of projecting away language-specific factors from a multilingual embedding space is provided and it is found that there exists a low-rank subspace that primarily encodes information irrelevant to semantics (e.g., syntactic information).

core.title: Beneath the Surface of Consistency: Exploring Cross-lingual Knowledge Representation Sharing in LLMs
affiliations: Weizmann Institute, EvalEval prev. MIT, IBM, Huji
core.venue: arXiv.org
core.summary: This work examines LLMs with various multilingual configurations using a new multilingual dataset and reveals that high consistency does not necessarily imply shared representation, particularly for languages with different scripts, and finds that script similarity is a dominant factor in representation sharing.

core.title: Linguistic Nepotism: Trading-off Quality for Language Preference in Multilingual RAG
core.venue: arXiv.org
core.summary: A controlled methodology using model internals to measure language preference while holding other factors such as document relevance constant is introduced, finding that models sometimes trade-off document relevance for language preference, indicating that citation choices are not always driven by informativeness alone.

core.title: Multilingual Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive Question Answering Task
core.venue: Conference of the European Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics

core.title: Learning Cross-Lingual IR from an English Retriever
core.venue: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics
core.summary: Dense Retrieval with Distillation-Enhanced Cross-Lingual Representation, a new cross-lingual information retrieval (CLIR) system trained using multi-stage knowledge distillation (KD), which demonstrates far superior accuracy over direct fine-tuning with labeled CLIR data.

core.title: Multilingual Retrieval Augmented Generation for Culturally-Sensitive Tasks: A Benchmark for Cross-lingual Robustness
core.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
core.summary: This work introduces BordIRLines, a dataset of territorial disputes paired with retrieved Wikipedia documents, across 49 languages and considers how RAG responses utilize presented documents, finding a much wider variance in the linguistic distribution of response citations, when querying in low-resource languages.

core.title: Hire a Linguist!: Learning Endangered Languages with In-Context Linguistic Descriptions
core.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
core.summary: This work proposes LINGOLLM, a training-free approach to enable an LLM to process unseen languages that hardly occur in its pre-training, and elevates translation capability from GPT-4's 0 to 10.5 BLEU for 10 language directions.

core.title: Multilingual Test-Time Scaling via Initial Thought Transfer
core.venue: arXiv.org
core.summary: The first systematic study of test-time scaling in multilingual settings is presented, evaluating DeepSeek-R1-Distill-LLama-8B and DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B across both high- and low-resource Latin-script languages.

core.title: Beyond Input Understanding: Diagnosing Multilingual Mathematical Reasoning with Directed Acyclic Trace Graphs
core.venue: arXiv.org
core.summary: DATG, a Directed Acyclic Trace Graph framework that maps reasoning traces to language-independent mathematical anchors and dependencies, is introduced and Loop-Retry and Formula-Retry are proposed, two simple test-time controls targeting DATG-exposed failure modes that consistently improve target-language reasoning performance in low-resource languages.

core.title: Rethinking Cross-lingual Alignment: Balancing Transfer and Cultural Erasure in Multilingual LLMs
core.venue: arXiv.org
core.summary: This work systematically analyze the cross-lingual alignment trade-off by introducing a holistic evaluation framework, the transfer-localization plane, which quantifies both desirable knowledge transfer and undesirable cultural erasure, and proposes Surgical Steering, a novel inference-time method that disentangles these two objectives.

core.title: Bridging the Language Gaps in Large Language Models with Inference-Time Cross-Lingual Intervention
core.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
core.summary: Inference-Time Cross-Lingual Intervention (INCLINE), a novel framework that enhances LLM performance on low-performing languages by aligning their internal representations with those of high-performing languages during inference, is proposed.

core.title: PolyWorkBench: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Cross-Lingual Long-Horizon Workflows
core.summary: Benchmark evaluations reveal that agent performance varies substantially across languages and drops sharply on the harder cross-lingual tasks, and analysis shows that multilingual execution exposes systematic failure modes across planning, tool interaction, and decision-making in long-horizon agents.

core.title: Lingua Franca or Probing Artifact? Rethinking Latent Language in Multilingual LLMs
core.summary: This work finds that identification probes systematically disagree: the GMM-based representation probe, which draws evidence from hidden state geometry, shows earlier cross-lingual mixing, whereas decoding-based probes, which rely on output-space decodability, retain sharper language-specific and more English-biased signals.

core.title: Language-Specific Neurons: The Key to Multilingual Capabilities in Large Language Models
core.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
core.summary: This paper delves into the composition of Transformer architectures in LLMs to pinpoint language-specific regions, and proposes a novel detection method, language activation probability entropy (LAPE), to identify language-specific neurons within LLMs.

core.title: Lost in Multilinguality: Dissecting Cross-lingual Factual Inconsistency in Transformer Language Models
affiliations: Centre for Information and Language Processing, LMU Munich
core.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
core.summary: This work uses mechanistic interpretability methods to investigate cross-lingual inconsistencies in MLMs and proposes a linear shortcut method that bypasses computations in the final layers, enhancing both prediction accuracy and cross-lingual consistency.

core.title: Challenges and Recommendations for LLM-as-a-Judge in Multilingual Settings and for Low-Resource Languages
core.summary: A checklist of recommendations about how to use LLM-as-a-Judge in multilingual and low-resource settings is concluded with a checklist of recommendations about how to use LLM-as-a-Judge in multilingual and low-resource settings.

core.title: Last Translation Benchmark
authors: L. D. M. S. Sai Teja
core.summary: The Last Translation Benchmark is introduced, a collection of human-authored and peer-reviewed examples that break leading machine translation models and a new evaluation approach: each example comes with handcrafted verification rules describing concrete failure cases on that example, therefore allowing reliable and actionable future evaluation.

core.title: Extending Item Response Theory for Efficient and Meaningful Multilingual Evaluation
core.venue: arXiv.org
core.summary: Fitting Multilingual-IRT on 25 LLMs across 29 languages of MMLU-Pro-X shows that its fitted parameters support three practical applications: predicting unobserved instances with 11-16% lower binary cross-entropy than the strongest accuracy-based baseline, surfacing candidate translation errors distributed across all 28 non-English languages, and recovering culture-specific items that accuracy-based baselines miss.

core.title: How do languages influence each other? Studying cross-lingual data sharing during LLM fine-tuning
core.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
core.summary: This study uses TracIn (Pruthi et al., 2020), a training data attribution (TDA) method, to retrieve the most influential training samples seen during multilingual fine-tuning for a particular test language and presents the first approach to study cross-lingual sharing at the data level.

core.title: Parameter Space Factorization for Zero-Shot Learning across Tasks and Languages
core.venue: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics
core.summary: A Bayesian generative model for the space of neural parameters is proposed that can be factorized into latent variables for each language and each task, and infer the posteriors over such latent variables based on data from seen task–language combinations through variational inference.

core.title: Code Mixologist : A Practitioner's Guide to Building Code-Mixed LLMs
core.venue: arXiv.org
core.summary: A unifying taxonomy is introduced that organizes prior work along dimensions of data, modeling, and evaluation, and distill these findings into a practical playbook of actionable recommendations for building, adapting, and evaluating CSW-capable LLMs.

core.title: Language Modeling for Code-Mixing: The Role of Linguistic Theory based Synthetic Data
core.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
core.summary: A computational technique for creation of grammatically valid artificial CM data based on the Equivalence Constraint Theory is presented and it is shown that when training examples are sampled appropriately from this synthetic data and presented in certain order, it can significantly reduce the perplexity of an RNN-based language model.

core.title: Understanding and Mitigating Language Confusion in LLMs
core.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
core.summary: The Language Confusion Benchmark (LCB) is created, which serves as a first layer of efficient, scalable multilingual evaluation and finds that language confusion can be partially mitigated via few-shot prompting, multilingual SFT and preference tuning.

core.title: Think Natively: Unlocking Multilingual Reasoning with Consistency-Enhanced Reinforcement Learning
core.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
core.summary: M-Thinker, which is trained by the GRPO algorithm that involves a Language Consistency (LC) reward and a novel Cross-lingual Thinking Alignment (CTA) reward, achieves nearly 100% language consistency and superior performance on two multilingual benchmarks, but also exhibit excellent generalization on out-of-domain languages.

core.title: Beyond the Rosetta Stone: Unification Forces in Generalization Dynamics
core.venue: arXiv.org
core.summary: This work introduces a controlled setting to study the causes and training dynamics of cross-lingual knowledge transfer by training small Transformer models from scratch on synthetic multilingual datasets and suggests methods to encourage representational unification as part of training that would improve LLMs'cross-lingual transfer.

core.title: How Do Multilingual Language Models Remember Facts?
Decolonising Speech and Language Technology
core.venue: International Conference on Computational Linguistics
core.summary: This paper reviews colonising discourses in speech and language technology, and suggests new ways of working with Indigenous communities, and seeks to open a discussion of a postcolonial approach to computational methods for supporting language vitality.
